title: The Net-Force Workshop
summary: Set gaps, rescale experiments, cancel forces on a probe and find balance points: work with Coulomb forces the way exam questions ask.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find a Coulomb force or gap, scale a force when charges or distance change, add forces by superposition and symmetry, and locate a point or set of charges in equilibrium.

levels.title: Set the gap
levels.adds: Baseline: solve F = kq₁q₂/r² for the gap (Ex 1.1, 1.2) and see that both charges feel equal, opposite forces.
hints: Rearrange Coulomb's law for the distance: r = √(k q₁ q₂ / F). Convert µC and cm to SI first.
Unlike charges pull together, like charges push apart.
The force on B is the same size as the force on A and points the opposite way (Newton's third law).

levels.title: Rescale
levels.adds: New idea: predict the new force when charges, the gap or sharing change (Ex 1.12, Example 1.4), without recalculating.
hints: F depends on q₁ × q₂ ÷ r². Work out how each change multiplies the force, then multiply them.
Halving the gap multiplies the force by 4, because r is squared.
Touching with an identical neutral sphere shares the charge equally, so each sphere keeps half.

levels.title: Null the probe
levels.adds: New idea: add forces as vectors and use symmetry so they cancel at a point (Ex 1.6, Examples 1.5 and 1.6).
hints: Each charge pulls or pushes the probe along the line joining them. Add those forces as vectors.
Charges at opposite corners are the same distance from the centre, so their forces lie on one line.
Two forces of the same size along one line cancel only if they point opposite ways.

levels.title: Rest on a line
levels.adds: New idea: find where two charges' forces cancel on a line, and which of three regions it must be in.
hints: Between like charges the forces point opposite ways, so they can cancel there. Between unlike charges they point the same way.
Outside two unlike charges, the balance point is nearer the weaker charge.
At the balance point the distances from A and B are in the ratio √|qA| : √|qB|.

levels.title: Everyone at rest
levels.adds: Harder: choose where a third charge goes and what charge it has so all three charges are in equilibrium.
hints: First find where the third charge itself feels no force, as in the previous level.
The held charges must also feel no net force. B pushes A away, so the third charge must pull A back: it needs the opposite sign.
Balance the forces on A: k qA qB / d² = k qA |q| / x². Solve for |q|.

misconceptions: Doubling the gap halves the force
The bigger charge pushes harder on the smaller one
Three equal charges around a point must pull it towards one of them
The balance point between two charges is the midpoint
